items.title: Week 47: Baltic clean index 2,581; one-year MR charter $34,000/day
items.summary: Compass Maritime's Nov 23 report puts the Baltic Clean Tanker Index at 2,581, against 2,592 a week earlier and 811 a year ago, while the dirty index rose to 5,081 from 4,483. Its one-year time-charter assessment for MRs eased to $34,000/day from $36,500, with LR1s unchanged at $53,500 and VLCCs down to $184,500 from $234,000.

items.title: Product tanker spot earnings down 4.8% on the week, led by Atlantic MRs
items.summary: Makai Research's week 47 report says product tanker spot earnings fell 4.8% week on week and are 13.4% below the late-October peak. MRs accounted for most of the decline, with Atlantic MR earnings falling sharply while Pacific MRs held near early-October levels; LRs slipped 2.1% and Handies were the only class to gain, on Med/Med business.

items.title: Hafnia drops pursuit of Torm; product tanker shares down 7.2% on week
items.summary: Nortilus reports that Hafnia has ended its pursuit of Torm. In week 47, listed product tanker equities fell 7.2% and crude tanker shares 4.3%, though both remain about 17% higher month to date; it also cites VLCC earnings down 18% to about $293,000/day.

items.title: Frontline Q3 profit $641.4m; Q4 LR2/Aframax booked at $190,800/day
items.summary: Frontline earned $641.4m ($2.88/share) in Q3 on revenue of $921.3m, including a $111.2m gain on two VLCC sales; adjusted profit was $530.9m versus $580.2m in Q2. For Q4 it has booked 68% of VLCC spot days at $562,600/day, 69% of Suezmax days at $324,300/day and 68% of LR2/Aframax days at $190,800/day, and says full-quarter rates will come in lower because of ballast days. Dividend is $2.38/share.

items.title: Large-tanker S&P: 2016-built VLCC sold for $210m
items.summary: Compass lists the 2016-built VLCC Bangladesh Prosperity (308,285 dwt) sold for $210m, a vessel it notes changed hands for $85.8m in October 2025, and the 2017-built Olympic Lady at $185m. In smaller sizes, the 2007-built Grand Ace6 (46,192 dwt) went for $20.5m and the 2023-built Bagshot (17,933 dwt) for $37.25m. Compass counts more than 90 VLCC sales so far in 2026 versus 50-plus in all of 2025; it values a 5-year-old MR at $53m.

items.title: Jones Act waiver extended a third time, to cargoes loaded by Feb 14
items.summary: DHS has extended the Jones Act waiver for 90 days from Nov 16; covered products must be loaded by 11:59 pm ET on Feb 14, 2027. The list of 237 HTS codes is unchanged and includes crude, refined products, LPG/LNG, fertilizers, ethyl alcohol for fuel, sulfur-based chemicals, anhydrous ammonia and biodiesel; the vessel-availability and reporting steps also stay the same.

items.title: Hanwha Philly cuts steel on first of four Jones Act MR chemical tankers
items.summary: Construction began Nov 17 on the first of four 49,500 dwt Jones Act MR product/chemical tankers for Hanwha Shipping, built to IMO Type 2 and 3 standards, with an optional 18-segregation configuration. Deliveries are scheduled for 2029–2030; Hanwha says it is the first US-built MR in nearly a decade.

items.title: Houthis threaten Jeddah and other Saudi Red Sea ports over Hodeidah
items.summary: The Houthis said Wednesday they would target Jeddah and all Saudi Red Sea ports if Saudi Arabia attacks Hodeidah, and urged shipping companies to withdraw vessels. The Saudi-led coalition said it struck targets at Hodeidah on Wednesday; on Tuesday a Houthi drone hit a Riyadh tower, injuring at least 11 people according to Saudi authorities.

items.title: Hormuz: UKMTO reports three vessels hit by projectiles; crews accounted for
items.summary: UKMTO said three vessels were struck by unidentified projectiles near the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, with all crew accounted for. The IRGC separately said it targeted a container ship near the strait; that claim was not independently confirmed in the report.

items.title: Ukrainian sea-drone attack at Benghazi naval base kills two Libyan officers
items.summary: Two Libyan naval officers died Tuesday of wounds from Sunday's Ukrainian drone attack on a Russian warship at the Benghazi naval base; Ukraine says seven sea drones were used. AP images show a cargo ship, Angara, and a capsized corvette at the base, and the eastern Libyan forces have vowed retaliation.

items.title: Houston Ship Channel: deep-draft transits up 12% in October
items.summary: Port Houston's November report shows 1,628 deep-draft transits in October (up 12% year on year) and 19,251 barge transits (down 2%). September foreign tonnage was 22.3m short tons, up 13%, with exports up 16%; the region handled 32% of US crude exports through September. Port Houston's terminals moved a record 415,326 TEU in October, up 14%.

items.title: Bunkers: Houston VLSFO $850.50/t, Fujairah $993.50/t
items.summary: Compass's Nov 23 report puts VLSFO at $850.50/t in Houston, $794.50 in Rotterdam, $993.50 in Fujairah and $1,019.50 in Singapore; MGO is $1,407.50/t in Houston.

items.title: Container and dry bulk: WCI $4,176/FEU, Capesizes $37,438/day
items.summary: Nortilus reports the Drewry World Container Index at $4,176 per 40ft, down 3% on the week, and Capesize earnings at $37,438/day, down 7.2%.

items.title: Tuesday Nov 24 close: Dow 50,018.70 (+0.85%), S&P 500 7,201.09 (−0.50%), Nasdaq −1.48%
items.summary: The Dow rose 423.39 points to close above 50,000, while the S&P 500 fell 36.08 points and the Nasdaq dropped 356.03 to 23,733.54 as chip stocks gave back part of Monday's gain; Nvidia fell 5.86%. Technology lost 3.26% and health care gained 2.95%. Figures are for Tuesday's session; Wednesday's session had not opened at publication.

items.title: Oil: Brent settles $91.40 (+2.27%), WTI $82.05 (+2.35%)
items.summary: Brent rose $2.03 and January WTI $1.88 on Tuesday as attacks on ships near the Strait of Hormuz and a Houthi strike on Riyadh added risk. Gains were limited by supply concerns: Deutsche Bank said October inventory builds imply a global surplus of about 1.7m b/d.

items.title: US natural gas up 15.3% to $3.671/MMBtu
items.summary: Henry Hub futures rose 15.30% Tuesday to $3.671/MMBtu, attributed to a cold snap and short-covering.

items.title: 10-year yield 4.90%; futures price about 95% odds of a December Fed hike
items.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield eased about 1 basis point to roughly 4.90% Tuesday, with the 2-year at 4.63% and the 30-year at 5.29%. CME FedWatch showed about 95–96% probability of a 25 bp rate increase at the December meeting, with the remainder on 50 bp.

items.title: Dollar index −0.47% to 103.83; gold −2.6%, silver −5.7%
items.summary: The dollar index fell to 103.83 Tuesday; EUR/USD was about 1.097 and USD/JPY about 159.18. Spot gold fell 2.64% to $3,555 and silver 5.65% to $40.71. The Conference Board's consumer confidence index came in at 103.3 versus a 92.5 consensus.

items.title: Abroad: Kospi +6.3%, Nikkei +3.9%; Stoxx 600 −0.7%
items.summary: On Tuesday Korea's Kospi rose 6.32% to 5,006.03 and Japan's Nikkei 225 gained 3.91% to 58,644.63, while the Hang Seng slipped 0.73%. In Europe the Stoxx 600 fell 0.66% to 632.74 and Germany's DAX 1.26% to 25,017.81.

items.title: Today: Q3 GDP, October PCE and jobless claims at 7:30 am CT
items.summary: The second estimate of Q3 GDP, October PCE inflation, personal income and spending, durable goods orders and weekly jobless claims are due Wednesday at 8:30 am ET (7:30 am CT). US markets are closed Thursday for Thanksgiving and close early, at 12:00 pm CT, on Friday.

items.title: Huawei convicted on 10 of 12 counts in Brooklyn federal trial
items.summary: A federal jury in Brooklyn found Huawei guilty on 10 of 12 counts, including bank fraud, sanctions violations and theft of trade secrets, and acquitted it of racketeering conspiracy. The trial ran more than two months.

items.title: Gaza: Israeli strikes kill at least nine, including Hamas security official
items.summary: Israeli strikes killed at least nine people from Monday night into Tuesday, including four in Shati camp; one was identified as an internal security official for Hamas in northern Gaza. Gaza's Health Ministry puts the war's death toll above 74,710.

items.title: Netanyahu and Kushner discuss Gaza humanitarian issues
items.summary: Prime Minister Netanyahu spoke by phone Tuesday with US envoy Jared Kushner about humanitarian conditions in Gaza, and both said they would keep working together. The call followed Kushner's public warning that Israel risked international isolation and the Board of Peace's criticism over its Hamas disarmament plan.

items.title: Sudan: drone strikes on Damazin kill at least 19
items.summary: Drone strikes on Damazin in Blue Nile state killed at least 19 people and wounded 15; a Sudanese lawyers' group blamed the RSF. Sudan's government also rejected an Ethiopian mediation offer.

items.title: Ukraine: death toll from strike on apartment block north of Kyiv reaches 11
items.summary: At least 11 people died in a Russian strike on an apartment building north of Kyiv, and a drone strike on a clinic in Zaporizhzhia killed at least three. German media reported NATO agencies warning that Russia could launch a nuclear-armed satellite by year end.

items.title: COP31 climate talks in Turkey end without agreement
items.summary: The COP31 negotiations in Turkey collapsed, with about 90 countries refusing to sign the outcome; the US did not take part.

items.title: Storms on both coasts threaten Thanksgiving travel
items.summary: More than 3,700 US flights were delayed Monday with a ground stop at Chicago O'Hare, and Delta said it had recovered from an automated-system outage. Pacific storms are bringing rain and mountain snow to the West, while a Gulf system may bring rain, wind and snow to the East.

items.title: Broncos (8–2) at Steelers Friday, 2:00 pm CT on Prime Video
items.summary: Denver is 8–2, tied with Kansas City for first in the AFC West. The Broncos play at Pittsburgh (6–4) on Black Friday, Nov 27, at 3:00 pm ET / 2:00 pm CT, streamed on Prime Video.

items.title: Texans (4–6) host Ravens Sunday at noon CT on CBS
items.summary: Houston is 4–6 and second in the AFC South behind Jacksonville (7–3). The Texans host Baltimore (4–7) on Sunday, Nov 29, at 1:00 pm ET / 12:00 pm CT on CBS.

items.title: Davis Cup: Czechia beats Canada 2–0 to reach Bologna semifinals
items.summary: Tomas Machac beat Liam Draxl 6-2, 3-6, 6-2 and Jiri Lehecka beat Felix Auger-Aliassime 7-6(4), 6-2, so the doubles was not needed. Canada played without Denis Shapovalov and Gabriel Diallo, who withdrew injured.

items.title: Davis Cup today: holders Italy face debutants South Korea
items.summary: Italy plays South Korea in a best-of-three quarterfinal in Bologna on Wednesday, Nov 25; the published schedule lists a 4:00 pm local (9:00 am CT) start. The winner meets Czechia in Friday's semifinal; Great Britain–Germany and Austria–Spain are scheduled for Thursday, and the final is Sunday, Nov 29.
